Subject: MSA redline: governing law + emergency remedies

Hi Sarah / Skyline procurement team —

Thanks for sending the draft MSA. We did a first pass and attached a redline (Skyline_MSA_v2_redline.docx) with a couple of open items we wanted to align on before legal ops prepares a final for signature. The two items blocking acceptance on our side are:

1) Governing law and seat for dispute resolution — the redline currently includes a general choice-of-law clause but the arbitration seat/venue is unspecified. For our footprint and enforcement, we prefer Delaware as governing law and New York as arbitration seat for commercial disputes, but we can be flexible if you have a strong reason.

2) Interim/emergency relief carveout — we need explicit language allowing either party to seek injunctive or provisional relief in court (to protect data, KV cache, and stop misuse) without waiving the arbitration requirement for the underlying dispute. We also want to avoid an overbroad waiver of bond/notice unless it meets our security checklist.

Concrete asks: can you confirm Skyline's position on (a) choice of law, (b) arbitration seat, and (c) whether you will accept a mutual emergency relief carveout referencing local courts where relief is sought?

I’ve cc’d Lauren and Karthik for legal/contracting input. If helpful we can jump on a 20-minute call tomorrow to settle this.

Regards,
Sooy (Soojin) Lee

Subject: Re: MSA redline: governing law + emergency remedies

Soojin —

Appreciate the clear note and your redline. Quick responses below (we included proposed language in the attached redline for clarity):

1) Governing law: Skyline generally prefers New York law for commercial agreements. We can accept Delaware only if Redwood specifically requires it — our legal team is willing to negotiate but NY law is our default.

2) Arbitration seat: We propose arbitration administered by ICDR with seat in New York, using a three-arbitrator panel for disputes >$2M and single arbitrator for smaller claims. We are open to expedited rules.

3) Interim relief / emergency remedies: We will agree to a carveout allowing either party to seek provisional or injunctive relief from a court of competent jurisdiction without waiving the arbitration agreement, but we want the clause to (a) require prompt notice to the other party where feasible, and (b) limit forum-shopping by specifying that courts in the state where the defendant is located are acceptable. We attached Emergency-Remedies-extract.pdf with our redline highlighting the carveout.

Two additional points:
- We cannot agree to a blanket waiver of bond for injunctive relief. We are willing to agree to a rebuttable presumption against requiring bond where the injunction is necessary to prevent irreparable harm to personal health data or operations, but language needs to be precise.
- If Redwood needs EU law or non-US seat for any subsidiary use-case, please flag now so we can propose a limited schedule for EU customers.

Happy to hop on a call — our team is available Wed afternoon for a 20–30 minute sync.

Best,
Sarah Jones
Associate General Counsel | Skyline Health
sarah.jones@skylinehealth.com

Subject: Re: MSA redline: governing law + emergency remedies

Sarah — thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposed language. A few internal clarifications from Redwood before we finalize:

1) Seat vs. governing law separation — we are ok with New York as the seat for arbitration provided that governing law can be Delaware (we prefer Delaware corporate law for predictability). Can you confirm Skyline counsel is open to that split? If not, we can accept NY law + NY seat as a compromise.

2) Injunctive relief carveout — we agree in principle with your wording but propose two tweaks: (i) allow Redwood to seek provisional relief in CA state or federal court where Redwood has operations without having to first demonstrate impossibility, and (ii) include a short-form confidentiality safe harbor for any emergency application so highly sensitive security details are protected.

3) Bond waiver — we understand Skyline’s concern. We can accept a limited presumption against bond where the moving party demonstrates a credible risk to personal data, system integrity, or imminent business-critical harm, subject to judicial discretion. Please confirm you can live with that middle ground.

If Skyline confirms the split (Delaware law / NY arbitration seat) and the mutual emergency carveout with the proposed tweaks, we will circulate an updated redline for legal ops to prepare for signature and procurement to issue the PO.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call today 11:00am PT to lock language.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Head of Legal Ops | Redwood Inference
